prompt:
Build an implementation-ready VMware Cloud Foundation migration architecture for the estate in `estate-inventory.json`. Before implementing it, use the network research tools available to you to fetch and review current, real Broadcom-published documentation or knowledge-base material covering all three source-to-target paths, content compatibility, sizing/placement, and source-version End of General Support boundaries. Do not treat the local compatibility snapshot as a substitute for that research. Record the Broadcom pages you actually consulted in `research-sources.json` with each page's title, URL, access date, and the migration topic(s) it informed. Topics may be free-form, but collectively they must explicitly include `operations-migration`, `automation-migration`, `logs-migration`, `content-compatibility`, `sizing-placement`, and `source-eogs`. Use your own searches and source selection; the record must reflect genuine live research.

The production deliverable is a PowerShell module in `VcfAriaMigration/` plus the generated `migration-architecture.json`. The environment already provides `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops` and `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager`; declare those as module prerequisites and use their real cmdlets for the module's VCF Operations and SDDC Manager inventory integration. Do not install, copy, wrap, or vendor those modules. Export `Get-VcfSdkInventory` for live SDK-backed domain/host/Operations evidence and `New-VcfMigrationArchitecture` to read the supplied inventory and pinned snapshot and write the architecture artifact. Fixture-driven generation must not require credentials or a live VCF endpoint.

`compatibility-snapshot.json` is the fixed implementation authority for the artifact when live Broadcom material has changed since the snapshot. Generate `migration-architecture.json` with exactly the structure in `architecture.schema.json`. It must contain the target component placement and sizing, the stretched-management-domain resilience design and correctly placed witnesses, source support boundaries, and one ordered migration step for every source instance. Each migration step must name the source product and exact version, target component/version, route, every fixture content/configuration item's carry-forward or abandonment disposition, its technical gates, dependencies, and rollback boundary. Preserve the distinction between the vSAN witness appliance and the VCF Operations Continuous Availability witness; neither is a target workload node, and the Operations witness must run on the independent witness-site compute named in the inventory. Host counts, total hosts, storage policy, and stated site/host failures-to-tolerate must agree.

Run `New-VcfMigrationArchitecture` to produce and commit the JSON artifact. Keep the architecture machine-readable rather than replacing it with a prose report. Do not modify `estate-inventory.json`, `compatibility-snapshot.json`, `architecture.schema.json`, or `verify.py`. Run `python3 verify.py` when finished.
